                    ### Question
                    A 63-year-old retired teacher presents to his family physician for an annual visit. He has been healthy for most of his life and currently takes no medications, although he has had elevated blood pressure on several visits in the past few years but declined taking any medication. He has no complaints about his health and has been enjoying time with his grandchildren. He has been a smoker for 40 years–ranging from half to 1 pack a day, and he drinks 1 beer daily. On presentation, his blood pressure is 151/98 mm Hg in both arms, heart rate is 89/min, and respiratory rate is 14/min. Physical examination reveals a well-appearing man with no physical abnormalities. A urinalysis is performed and shows microscopic hematuria. Which of the following is the best next step for this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Reassure the patient and recommend lifestyle modifications for his hypertension
opb. Perform a CT scan of the abdomen with contrast
opc. Perform intravenous pyelography
opd. Perform a cystoscopy
ope. Repeat the urinalysis

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with elevated blood pressure and microscopic hematuria, which raises concern for potential urinary tract issues, particularly given his long history of smoking, a known risk factor for urinary tract cancers. While lifestyle modifications for hypertension are important, the presence of hematuria necessitates further investigation to rule out serious conditions such as malignancy. A CT scan of the abdomen with contrast is often preferred as an initial imaging modality because it provides comprehensive information about the kidneys and urinary tract, making it a suitable next step. Cystoscopy, while useful for direct visualization of the bladder, is more invasive and typically reserved for cases where imaging suggests bladder pathology. Therefore, the best next step is to perform a CT scan of the abdomen with contrast to evaluate the underlying causes of hematuria.
